references.quote: In ATP III, low HDL cholesterol was defined categorically as a level <40 mg/dL (raised from <35 mg/dL).

references.quote: A1C >=6.5% (48 mmol/mol) defines diabetes; A1C 5.7-6.4% (39-47 mmol/mol) identifies increased risk (prediabetes).

why: Long-term (2-3 month) glycemic control marker; ADA normal <5.7%, prediabetes 5.7-6.4%, diabetes >=6.5%.

refDefault.note: No formal guideline diagnostic threshold. Reference-lab fasting interval (Labcorp) 2.6-24.9 µIU/mL. Many metabolic clinicians consider <5-9 µIU/mL metabolically optimal (heuristic, not guideline).

references.quote: Fasting serum insulin reference interval approximately 2.6-24.9 µIU/mL.

why: Fasting insulin gauges pancreatic beta-cell output and insulin resistance. No consensus diagnostic cutoff; interpreted against a reference-lab interval (2.6-24.9 µIU/mL) and, orientationally, lower-is-better for metabolic health.

references.document: LOINC 62418-9 Glucose/Insulin [Ratio] in Serum or Plasma
references.quote: Glucose/Insulin [Ratio] in Serum or Plasma — a derived index used to screen for insulin resistance (e.g., in PCOS).

why: Derived index (fasting glucose divided by fasting insulin), not a standard measured analyte. Lower ratios suggest insulin resistance; cutoffs (e.g., <4.5 mass-ratio, or the printed >10) are lab/assay-specific and not backed by a formal guideline, so refDefault is null and evidence is heuristic.
